html:
The map's "Emirate of Bin Shal'an", shown from 1920 to 1938, is named after the Sha'lan family, the leading chiefs of the Ruwala, a large Bedouin tribe of the Anizzah confederation in the deserts of northern Arabia and Syria.

In the early 1900s the Ruwala chief Nuri al-Sha'lan was one of the strongest desert rulers, holding the oasis of al-Jawf. In 1918 he joined the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans, alongside T. E. Lawrence. In 1922 Ibn Saud took al-Jawf.

The map's shape for this emirate covers much of inner Arabia, which in these years was in fact ruled by Ibn Saud, so the label is best read loosely.
